ai.definition: A brain-computer interface that decodes intended speech from neural signals to enable communication for individuals who are unable to speak.
ai.howItWorks: Electrode arrays placed over the speech-motor cortex record neural activity, which is then translated by machine-learning models into words or text. This process often includes visual feedback through an on-screen avatar of a speaking head.
ai.problemSolved: Restores communication for individuals with paralysis, ALS, and other conditions that impair speech abilities.
ai.manufacturing: Involves the development and integration of electrode arrays, signal processing hardware, and machine-learning algorithms. Requires precise manufacturing techniques to ensure accurate recording and translation of neural signals.
ai.buildProcess: Includes the design and testing of electrode arrays, calibration of the system with individual users, training of machine-learning models on user-specific data, and integration of visual feedback systems.
ai.costDrivers: High costs associated with electrode array development, signal processing hardware, and specialized personnel for system calibration and maintenance. Significant investment in machine-learning model training and validation.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to transition from clinical trials to broader adoption as technology matures and more users gain access.
ai.regulation: Subject to regulatory approval processes, including clinical trial approvals, device certification, and post-market monitoring. Requires compliance with healthcare regulations governing medical devices and patient data privacy.
ai.risks: Technical risks related to electrode array performance, signal-to-noise ratio, and machine-learning model accuracy. Ethical concerns around user privacy, data security, and potential misuse of the technology.
ai.profitability: Potential for high profitability once the technology gains market acceptance and widespread use in clinical settings. However, initial costs and regulatory hurdles may limit short-term revenue generation.
ai.futureDevelopment: Expected to see advancements in electrode array design, miniaturization of hardware components, improvements in machine-learning algorithms, and integration with other BCI technologies for enhanced functionality.

glossary.def: Brain-computer interface, a system that enables direct communication between the brain and external devices.
A condition characterized by the loss of muscle function in a body part or limb.
